material_definitions: In order to better understand the effect of aliovalent doping in Li+ conducting argyrodites, the substitution of P5+ with Si4+ was performed in the solid solutions Li(6+x)P(1-x)Si(x)S5X.

By combining structural characterizations, i.e. X-ray and neutron diffraction with electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, the effect of increasing the Si4+ content on the ionic conductivity was shown.
The larger Si4+ increases the size of the unit cell, and also increases the Li+ concentration and leads to a rising occupancy of Li+ on the transition state for hopping.
The materials investigated are the solid solution series Li(6+x)P(1-x)Si(x)S5Br, belonging to the argyrodite superionics class.
Ionic conductivity measurements were performed via temperature-dependent impedance spectroscopy.
Substitution of P5+ by Si4+ increases the mobile Li+ content, resulting in increased bulk conductivity.
The highest room-temperature conductivity of 2.4 mS/cm was observed for x = 0.35.
The change in conductivity is potentially related to enhanced Li+-Li+ correlation, as the activation energy remains relatively unchanged.
